title: Chapter 236: Four New Members
html:
The elevator finally opened on the twelfth floor, the midpoint of the building.

The ritual is over, but the twenty-fourth floor never appeared.

The doors opened onto a dark corridor. Remaining inside the elevator, Chen Ge took out the Ghost Stories Society’s flyer. The first floor corresponds to the twenty-third, and the second corresponds to the twenty-second. But the twelfth lies exactly in the middle; it has no counterpart.

Chen Ge thought about it but could not be sure whether he had been successful or not. Is it because of the old woman? Is that why I failed? Should I try again?

It was already Wednesday. Standing in the elevator and staring out, Chen Ge felt deeply unsettled. “The display can show twenty-four floors, but the panel has no button for the twenty-fourth. Is that an installation error, or does it mean something else?”

Unwilling to give up, Chen Ge decided to return to the top floor. He selected the twenty-third, and the elevator began climbing without stopping.

20, 21, 22…

Chen Ge watched the display. When 22 changed to 23, the elevator did not slow as it had before. The red number darkened as though bleeding. A cold gust gathered inside the sealed car, and strange sounds rose beyond its walls.

Chen Ge braced himself in the corner, body half-curled, fingers reaching toward the cleaver on his calf. After roughly two seconds, the elevator began to slow. When it stopped completely, a new number illuminated the display.

The 24th floor!

The silver-gray doors opened. As the halves drew apart, a sticky substance resembling blood stretched between them. A wave of stench flooded the car. Covering his nose and mouth, Chen Ge recognized it immediately; he had smelled something similar at Hai Ming Apartments and the Third Sick Hall.

This smell seems to be unique to the monsters behind the door!

Once the doors had fully opened, Chen Ge stared down the corridor and hesitated. Rather than stepping out, he assigned Gu Feiyu’s number to speed dial. This added a step before the police could be called, but it also prevented an emergency call from revealing Chen Ge’s identity.

After completing the setup, Chen Ge took another object from his pocket—something he had debated bringing from the Haunted House.

The flyer requires every member to conceal their identity behind a mask.

Chen Ge’s Haunted House contained many masks, but he was most comfortable with Doctor Skull-cracker’s skin mask. This should make it easier to blend in with a group of lunatics.

Wearing it outside the Haunted House felt strange, but this was no time to worry about appearances.

After stepping out, Chen Ge looked back. Bloody smears and handprints covered the walls beside the elevator, as though people had struggled to crawl toward it only to be dragged mercilessly away.

The elevator slowly closed, and it did not return after it left.

How am I supposed to leave?

There had to be another way out. That was the only reassurance Chen Ge could offer himself. He checked his equipment, then started down the corridor.

Inside the elevator, he had heard people screaming. Now that he stood outside, however, the floor was suspiciously quiet. Every door was locked, and no sound escaped from within.

It doesn’t seem like there is anyone alive on this floor.

As he moved forward, the light dimmed, and more blood stains appeared on the wall.

Will the society be in one of these rooms?

After roughly ten meters, Chen Ge found an open door. He edged toward it and was about to look inside when a person in a bird mask suddenly emerged.

Chen Ge froze, but the bird-masked figure recoiled as though startled. Chen Ge remained silent. In an unfamiliar environment, every word risked exposing him.

Both were silent. After several breaths, the birdman asked with suspicion, “A new member?”

“Yes.” Chen Ge lowered his voice and made it rougher.

“But three new members have already arrived tonight. Why is there a fourth?” The bird-masked man blocked Chen Ge’s path. “How did you find this place?”

Chen Ge showed him the Ghost Stories Society flyer. The man glanced at it, and his curiosity deepened. “This is one of ours, but how can there be a fourth invitee?”

He leaned toward Chen Ge until the beak on his mask was almost touching Chen Ge’s face.

“You smell nice…” The birdman closed the door behind him and said with uncertainty, “Come with me.”

Chen Ge followed with his head lowered, his eyes twitching. As the bird-masked man closed the door, Chen Ge stole a glance inside. Several wooden crates sat in the darkness. One remained unsealed, and an arm protruded from it. A circular wound pierced the center of its palm, as though made by a bird’s beak.

Following the birdman, they reached the end of the corridor.

“Go in.” He pointed at the door at the end of the corridor.

“Okay.”

Chen Ge did not waste time. He opened the door, waited two seconds to ensure no ambush awaited him, then stepped inside. The sight before him made him draw a sharp breath.

The room was larger than expected. A long dining table occupied its center. Ten figures in blank masks and dark robes sat along its sides—five on the left and five on the right. Three casually dressed people stood nearby.

Thirteen of them…

Within seconds, Chen Ge memorized every person’s distinguishing features. Is it the lighting? Why do the five on the right cast shadows while the five on the left do not?

“Get in, our fourth new member. Good luck.” The birdman did not give Chen Ge any chance to run and slammed the door shut.

The sound was loud, and it attracted the attention of everyone in the room. All the masks turned toward Chen Ge.

“Why is there a fourth new member?” The man in the first seat on the right stood. His voice was sharp, and a cigarette burn marked his exposed little finger.

“Do not interrupt someone’s story,” the first person on the left said in a faded tone. He sounded disgruntled.

“But how can there be four?” The man on the right returned to his seat.

“It doesn’t matter. In the end, only three will remain,” the man on the left said darkly. The three newcomers standing beside the table immediately tensed.
